beats.text: Namaste! This video introduces ToolTrace: a smart system to track tools and their calibration on the factory floor.
You will see the problem it solves, how to use it step by step, its main features, and the benefits for your company.
First, the problem.
In most plants, tools are tracked in a paper register or an Excel sheet.
Tools go missing, and nobody can say who took the torque wrench last Tuesday.
A tool whose calibration has expired can still be used on a job, because nothing stops it. That is a quality risk.
Entries are made late, or not at all. And when an auditor asks for proof, someone spends hours searching through files.
Lost tools are bought again, and jobs wait while people search. All of this costs time and money.
ToolTrace replaces the register with one simple web app. It works on a computer at the tool crib, and on any phone on the shop floor.
Every tool gets a QR label, and if you like, an RFID tag. So the app always knows where each tool is, who has it, and when it is due back.
beats.say: Every tool gets a QR label, and if you like, an R-F-I-D tag. So the app always knows where each tool is, who has it, and when it is due back.

beats.text: There are four roles. The admin manages people and settings. The storekeeper runs the tool crib.
The technician takes tools for jobs. And the auditor can see everything, but cannot change anything.
Now, let us see how to use it.
This is the sign-in page. Real users sign in with a passkey: their fingerprint, face, or phone PIN. There are no passwords to forget or steal.
This demo also has one-click roles. We will start as Ravi, the storekeeper.
This is the tool board. It works like a shadow board on the wall: every tool has its own place.
The top line shows how many tools are out, how many are overdue, and how many are locked.
A solid card means the tool is in the crib. A dotted outline means it is out, and shows who has it and when it is due back.
Overdue tools are marked in red. A small square in the corner warns that calibration is due soon, or has expired.
With one click, you can see only the tools that need attention.
To issue a tool, the storekeeper opens it, and picks the person.
Then chooses when it should come back, and clicks Check out.
Done. The board now shows who has the tool. The time and the storekeeper's name are saved automatically.
When a tool comes back, the storekeeper opens it, and notes its condition: good, damaged, or needs calibration.
Here, the ratchet is slipping, so we mark it as damaged and click Receive.
A damaged tool is quarantined automatically. Nobody can take it until it is repaired and checked.
Now, calibration. This torque wrench is past its calibration date, so ToolTrace has locked it.
Not only the screen: the server and the database itself refuse to issue it. There is no way around this rule.
After the tool is calibrated, the storekeeper records who calibrated it, and the certificate number.
The tool is unlocked at once, and the next due date is set automatically.
The Tools page lists every tool. You can search by tag or name, and filter by status or calibration.
For example, here are the tools whose calibration is due soon, so they can be planned in time.
Adding a new tool takes a few seconds. Then print its QR label, and stick it on the tool.
Now, the technician's view, on a phone. Asha signs in.
Her screen shows the tools she has, and when each one is due back.
To take a tool, she taps Scan, and points the camera at the QR label. She can also type the tag.
She chooses when she will return it, and taps Check out. It takes about ten seconds.
Sometimes there is no network signal on the shop floor. ToolTrace keeps working.
The check-out is saved on the phone.
When the signal returns, it is sent automatically, exactly once. Nothing is lost, and nothing is counted twice.
For even faster work, the crib can have a smart station: a small RFID reader built on an ESP32 board.
beats.say: For even faster work, the crib can have a smart station: a small R-F-I-D reader, built on an E S P 32 board.

beats.text: The admin adds a station here. Each station gets its own secret key.
Now watch the board. Asha taps her ID badge at the station, and then taps the tool.
That's it. No typing at all. And every open screen updates live, at the same moment, without refreshing.
Every message from a station is digitally signed. A fake or altered message is rejected, and recorded.
Every night, a machine learning model studies all past check-outs.
For each tool that is out right now, it shows the risk of a late return or a loss, with the reasons in plain words.
It also flags unusual check-outs: for example, a tool taken in the middle of the night, or kept much longer than usual.
A person reviews each flag, and decides. The model only gives an early warning; it never blames anyone.
The admin manages people. To add someone, enter their email and role, and click Create invite.
Share the link or QR code. They create their passkey, and they are in.
When someone leaves, one click deactivates them, and signs them out on every device.
Finally, the audit trail. Every action is recorded: who did what, and when.
Each record is sealed with a cryptographic hash of the one before, like links in a chain.
Click Verify integrity, and ToolTrace proves that no record was changed or deleted. Even the database owner cannot quietly rewrite history.
Here are the key features at a glance.
A live tool board. Check-out by QR code, RFID badge, or from the crib. A calibration lock. And offline mode.
beats.say: A live tool board. Check-out by QR code, R-F-I-D badge, or from the crib. A calibration lock. And offline mode.

beats.text: Smart stations. Nightly insights. Passkey sign-in, with a role for each person. And a tamper-proof audit trail.
So, how is this better than a register or an Excel sheet?
With a register, you know where a tool is only if someone wrote it down. With ToolTrace, you know in real time.
A register cannot stop an expired tool from being used. ToolTrace blocks it.
A register can be changed, or lost. In ToolTrace, any change to a record is detected.
And a register only tells you the past. ToolTrace warns you early, before a tool goes late or missing.
Now, the key benefits for the company.
One. Fewer lost tools, and less money spent on replacing them.
Two. Better quality. Only calibrated tools reach the job, which supports quality standards and customer audits.
Three. Time saved. Issuing a tool takes seconds, and audit evidence is ready in minutes, not days.
Four. Clear accountability. At every moment, each tool has one named person responsible for it.
Five. Better decisions. Usage data shows which tools are in demand, and which are rarely used, to plan purchases wisely.
Six. Strong security. No passwords to steal, access based on roles, and records that cannot be faked.
And seven. Low cost. It runs in a browser on the computers and phones you already have, and the stations use low-cost parts.
Getting started is simple.
Step one: add your tools, and stick on the QR labels. Step two: invite your team.
Step three: start with one tool crib as a pilot. Then, roll it out to the other areas of the plant.
Thank you for watching! Try the live demo yourself at tooltrace-vijayant.vercel.app. Pick a role, and explore.
